newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt's 1995/6 exports down, imports up.
newsitem.headline: Egypt's 1995/6 exports down, imports up.

text.p: The value of Egyptian exports fell 7.3 percent in the financial year 1995/6, to $4.593 billion from $4.957 billion in the previous year, according to a central bank report prepared for parliament. The years start July 1.
The value of imports rose 7.9 percent, to $13.827 billion from $12.810 billion in 1994/5, it said.
The trade deficit rose 17.6 percent to a record $9.234 billion, from $7.853 billion in the previous year.
But the government newspaper al-Ahram said the balance of payments remained in surplus at $577 million. The surplus in 1994/5 was $754 million, the central bank said last year.

Al-Ahram said this pushed the country's foreign reserves up to $18.5 billion at the end of June 1996. The central bank said last year that they stood at between $18.2 billion and $18.3 billion at the end of June 1995.

Egypt traditionally runs a large trade deficit but a surplus on services and transfers -- tourism, Suez Canal receipts and remittances from Egyptians abroad -- keeps the current account roughly in balance. Net capital flows are usually positive.

The trade figures showed that exports in the fourth quarter of 1995/6 -- the April-June quarter -- were however 9.2 percent up on the same period of the previous year, at $1.313 billion compared with $1.202 billion.
Exports in that quarter were 9.8 percent higher, at $3.706 billion compared with $3.374 billion.
